claims: The store is MECHANICALLY reindex-free: appending new content mutates no fitted artifact.

Appending is behaviourally near-free for new ENTITIES but not for new RELATIONS, AT DEPTH 1: head new entity +0.058, new relation +0.191. At DEPTH 2 the penalty is +0.249 and 'near-free' does not hold at all.

The store LEARNS: of the questions it properly REFUSED before an update, 432 of 432 (1.000) are answered correctly after it. Separately, it properly refused only 432 of the 1179 it could not answer (0.366); 21 of the 1200 were already answerable.

The store REVISES rather than going stale: after a superseding edit it almost never keeps asserting the old fact — 1 of 431 previously-old-answering cases stays old (0.002). Revision is 0.459; the dominant failure is refusal (0.348) and wrong answers (0.190), not staleness.
Revision is two operations: editing a fact alone revises 0.469 of previously-correct answers with 0.274 breakage; editing it AND supplying the edges its new target needs revises 0.733 with 0.077.
Composition generalises to relation pairs never seen composed: at depth 2 held-out pairs score 0.9245 against trained pairs' 0.9135, a difference of +0.011 in the held-out pairs' FAVOUR.

The STORE supplies what makes multi-hop answering work, and the step-by-step WALK does not: an exhaustive planner allowed to consult the store for which chains are walkable scores 0.9032 against the walker's 0.9123 (inside its CI), while the same planner denied the store scores 0.3883. Availability filtering is worth +0.515; greedy walking is worth +0.009.
Depth extrapolates without depth-specific training for ANSWERING at 3 hops: 0.849 with no 3-hop in training, against 0.961 when 3-hop IS trained.

On a MIXED unanswerable benchmark the answer-type gate lifts not-applicable refusal from 0.050 to 0.693, and cuts DEPTH-1 answerable wrongness from 0.118 to 0.045 (depth-2, separately, 0.175 to 0.102).

Refusal is governed by the MOST confusable option available at the break step, not by how many options there are. With branching held identical across arms, refusal tracks the maximum cosine between an available relation and the asked one at r=-0.954, against -0.774 for the mean and -0.485 for the count; ONE confusable option refuses 0.8485 while EIGHT non-confusable ones refuse 0.8848.

Compression buys generalisation and costs REFUSAL, not the accuracy of what it enables. Under one threshold protocol, a frozen K=48 basis takes novel-relation answering from 0.0054 to 0.7419 while its wrong-rate moves only 0.1531 to 0.1667 — raw's low score is raw REFUSING (abstain 0.8415), not raw erring. At matched coverage the gain is +0.7407 correct for +0.0723 wrong, a tenth of the gain; the real costs are refusal on novel unanswerables (-0.7060), refusal on known ones (-0.5685) and known-relation answering (-0.1409 at 9x the wrong-rate).

Alias supply explains MOST of retrieval's advantage over a parametric head, and not all of it: the gap falls 0.229 -> 0.042 over 2 to 10 aliases, and on the population where supply reaches 18 it stops falling at ~0.09 (0.087 at 10, 0.091 at 18, tail slope +0.0015/alias). The residual is a capability difference, not a supply shortfall.

Claim adjudication is noisy in a specific, measurable way: instability is concentrated in ONE rater (flags per identical run 6/7/4, range 3, against ranges of 1, 1 and 2 for the other three), and the two prompts disagree completely at quorum — verification flagged 0 of 14 while attack flagged 6 of 14, with two claims flagged only by attack and one only by verification.
Entities are free for the parametric head and expensive for retrieval: subjects held out of training score 0.766 against seen subjects' 0.795 at depth 1, while retrieval drops from 0.854 to 0.526.

9.falsifier: The falsifier is refusal changing with count while maximum cosine is fixed; the confusable arm does exactly that, falling from 0.8485 to 0.7758.
At fixed maximum cosine, refusal could still vary materially with option count; the confusable arm already falls from 0.8485 to 0.7758 as count rises.
Case-level controlled variation could make count more predictive than maximum cosine; correlations across aggregated cells with coupled manipulations do not rule that out.
Claim says count does not govern, but with max-cos pinned the confusable arm still drops 0.8485→0.7758 as k grows; also 'any store' is untested.

Falsifier: count tracks refusal better than max cosine on ANY store, or arms fail cosine separation. Here max_cos r=-0.954 beats count, separation 0.1539, but one-corpus/fixed-THR/≥8-option filter doe

Falsifier ‘tracks count better than max-cos on any store’ is untested beyond one corpus/THR. Also 1 confusable refuses less than 8 non-confusable (0.849 vs 0.885), so the headline contrast does not se

11.falsifier: The falsifier is the gap resuming its decline beyond 18 aliases; no measurements beyond 18 rule that out, so the residual cannot yet be assigned to capability.
The gap could resume shrinking beyond 18 aliases; no measurements beyond 18 rule out continued supply-driven convergence, so the residual is not established as capability.
The gap could resume falling beyond 18 aliases; no measurement beyond 18 rules this out, so the claimed permanent capability residual is unsupported.
The data artificially stops at 18 aliases, making it impossible for the supplied evidence to rule out the gap falling further at higher supplies.
The supplied evidence stops at 18 aliases, meaning it is impossible to rule out the falsifier of the gap resuming its fall past 18.
Falsifier is gap resuming after 18 aliases; tail is only three noisy points on 8 relations, so 'stops'/'capability residual' is not closed.

Falsifier: gap keeps falling past 18 aliases, or head matches 1-NN at some supply. Plateau ~0.09 on n=8 relations only; noise_half_width 0.026 and tiny set leave room gap is still falling or selection
Falsifier ‘gap resumes falling past 18’ is not ruled out—curve only reaches 18 on the 8-rel set. ‘Stops falling / residual is capability’ overclaims a short plateau (noise_half_width 0.026).

12.falsifier: The falsifier is non-disjoint quorum flag sets; the supplied artifact does not provide both quorum sets, and verification flagging 0/14 contradicts the claimed verification-only item.
Verification quorum flagging any claim or overlapping attack would falsify it; claim 12 has verification votes from two quorum raters and is also attack-flagged.
Prompt overlap or non-concentrated instability would falsify it; the supplied artifact omits attack-run details and its 0-versus-6 quorum statement cannot support claims unique to verification.
Claim 12 received two verification votes at quorum and was also flagged by attack, meaning the sets overlap and the falsifier is triggered.
Falsifier triggers because the attack prompt and verification prompt flag overlapping sets (e.g., item 12 is flagged by both).
The evidence shows verification flagged claim 12 at quorum (gpt and grok), directly overlapping with the attack prompt's flags and triggering the falsifier.
Claim says verification quorum flags 0/14 yet also 'one only by verification'; attack-vs-verification split is not evidenced cleanly enough to rule out overlap/contradiction.

Falsifier: within-rater ranges comparable, or prompt flag sets overlap. Ranges 3 vs 1/1/2 and attack vs verification quorum split are in the table, but attack-prompt totals are not in the supplied JSO
Claim contradicts itself (verification quorum 0/14 vs ‘one flagged only by verification’); attack arm numbers are absent from evidence; claim-12 has 2/3 verification votes so ‘verification flagged 0’

scope: Per-rater majority of 3 adversarial runs, then quorum over raters outside the author's model family. SPLIT means a rater returned three different verdicts on identical input and is reported, not resolved. The verification pass is listed separately and never merged with attack: the two prompts reward opposite behaviours, so a claim passing one and failing the other is a finding about the claim, not rater noise. Every artifact was checked against the current claim text before use; misaligned ones are listed in `excluded_artifacts` and contribute nothing.
